previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of heavy alcohol use, was admitted for chest pain and alcohol withdrawal. The chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, likely from a recent fall, with no evidence of acute cardiac event. He underwent alcohol detoxification with diazepam and supportive vitamins. During the stay, he developed vertigo, which was diagnosed as benign paroxysmal positional vertigo and treated with an Epley maneuver. Persistent nausea and vomiting led to an endoscopy, which revealed gastritis, prompting an increase in omeprazole. His heart failure and atrial fibrillation were managed with continued and adjusted medications, including restarting verapamil. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for follow-up, alcohol counseling, and close monitoring of weight and symptoms.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with a PMHx of alcohol abuse 
and CAD who presented with chest pain and intoxication.

# Chest pain: 
Given Mr. ___ prior history of STEMI in ___, there was 
considerable concern for recurrent MI, however cardiac enzymes 
and EKG were reassuring. He was continued on home beta blocker, 
statin and aspirin. CT of the chest and abdomen were also 
negative for PE and aortic dissection. His pain was ultimately 
felt to be musculoskeletal in nature as it worsened with arm 
movement and was reproducible to palpation.

# Alcohol Withdrawal: 
Patient was intoxicated on admission with ETOH level of 487. 
CIWA protocol was later initiated with diazepam for signs of 
withdrawal. Patient was encouraged to seek substance abuse 
treatment, however, was not amenable at this time to rehab 
placement.

# CHF, chronic AFib s/p ICD:
EF ___ secondary to ischemic, tachycardia induced or 
alcoholic cardiomyopathy. Patient showed no evidence of acute 
decompensation. He was continued on home lasix and losartan. 
Patient remained in sinus rhythm during his course. He was 
continued on verapamil and metoprolol. Patient reported 
non-compliance with anticoagulation. 

# HTN:
Continued home antihypertensive regimen.

# PE ___:
Patient reported non-compliance with Dabigatran, although the 
details surrounding his diagnosis, including planned course of 
anticoagulation remained unclear. As noted above, chest CT on 
this admission revealed no acute PE, although did note changes 
in the right lower lobe consistent with prior PE and pulmonary 
infarction.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Chest pain and shortness of breath in patient with alcohol
intoxication and history of pulmonary embolism.  The patient also has left
subcostal pain and left upper quadrant abdominal pain.

COMPARISON:  CT of the torso from ___ and CTA of the chest from
___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images of the chest were obtained first
without contrast and then in the early arterial phase after administration of
100 cc of Omnipaque contrast material.  Next, the abdomen was scanned in the
portal venous phase.  Coronal, sagittal, and pulmonary arterial oblique images
also reviewed.

FINDINGS:

CTA CHEST:  There are no pulmonary arterial filling defects to suggest
presence of pulmonary embolism.  A right lower lobe segmental artery tapers
distally, leading to a wedge shaped peripheral scar from the patient's prior
pulmonary embolism and pulmonary infarction.  The aorta is of normal caliber,
without evidence of dissection.

CT CHEST:  The visualized thyroid gland appears normal.  There is no
supraclavicular, axillary, mediastinal, or hilar lymphadenopathy.  The
tracheobronchial tree appears normal.  The lungs are clear aside from the scar
in the right lower lobe.  The heart is minimally enlarged and there is no
pericardial or pleural effusion.  There is no pneumothorax.

CT ABDOMEN:  There are two subcentimeter liver hypodensities which are
unchanged from prior studies dating back to ___ (3b:108, 100). 
These are too small to characterize.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic
biliary ductal dilation.  The gallbladder appears normal.  The pancreas,
spleen and adrenal glands appear normal.  The stomach and visualized loops of
small and large bowel are unremarkable.  There is no intra-abdominal fluid
collection or free air.  The abdominal aorta is normal.  There is no
retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  The bilateral kidneys enhance
normally, without hydronephrosis.  Evaluation of the osseous structures
reveals no acute fracture or evidence of other traumatic injury.  There are no
lytic or blastic lesions concerning for malignancy.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of acute aortic syndrome or pulmonary embolism.
2.  No evidence of traumatic injury to the abdomen.
